speaker: Unknown
en: I experimented with psychedelics when I was young.
zh: 我年轻时尝试过致幻剂。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm 70 now.
zh: 我现在 70 岁了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it very much informed my view of the world, or view of reality, or view of civilizations, structures, and all of that.
zh: 而这在很大程度上塑造了我对世界的看法,或者对现实的看法,或者对文明、结构以及所有这些东西的看法。

speaker: Unknown
en: But could it simply be the suppression of the self and the resulting experience?
zh: 但这可能仅仅是自我的压制以及由此产生的体验吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: It's just your brain.
zh: 那只是你的大脑。

speaker: Unknown
en: In the case of psychedelics, it's your brain on drugs.
zh: 就致幻剂而言,那是你的大脑在药物作用下的状态。

speaker: Unknown
en: OK, so all it teaches us that brains can reach extraordinary states.
zh: 好,那么它教会我们的仅仅是大叔可以进入非凡的状态。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you have someone
zh: 如果你有人

speaker: Unknown
en: In a vegetative state and it's been declared in a vegetative state and you use this device and detect that there is complex neural activity that suggests consciousness.
zh: 处于植物人状态,并且被判定为植物人状态,而你使用这个设备检测到存在暗示意识的复杂神经活动。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you pull the life support on that picture, do you see some spike in complexity that might correlate to their recognition of what's happening?
zh: 如果你在这个画面中撤掉生命维持系统,你会看到某种复杂性的飙升,可能与他们对正在发生的事情的认知相关联吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: We now know that a quarter of these patients, one out of four of these patients is actually conscious.
zh: 我们现在知道,这些病人中有四分之一,四分之一实际上是有意识的。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're there.
zh: 他们在那里。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're present.
zh: 他们在场。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're just not able to signal it.
zh: 他们只是无法发出信号表达。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you lose the cerebellum, it's not good for you.
zh: 如果你失去了小脑,这对你不好。

speaker: Unknown
en: Cerebellum is there to do sensory motor coordination among others.
zh: 小脑的存在,除其他功能外,是为了做感觉运动协调。

speaker: Unknown
en: But people never complain that if lesion in the cerebellum, never complain about loss of consciousness.
zh: 但人们从来不会抱怨小脑损伤会导致意识丧失,从不抱怨意识的丧失。

speaker: Unknown
en: It doesn't seem to relate to consciousness because it's not very well integrated.
zh: 它似乎与意识无关,因为它没有被很好地整合。

speaker: Unknown
en: Everything is mental.
zh: 一切都是心理的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Everything is phenomenal.
zh: 一切都是现象的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Everything ultimately is consciousness.
zh: 一切归根结底都是意识。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm a physicist.
zh: 我是物理学家。

speaker: Unknown
en: I got my PhD in theoretical physics, but I studied for the past 40 years brains.
zh: 我拿到了理论物理的博士学位,但过去 40 年我研究的是大脑。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm a neuroscientist.
zh: 我是一名神经科学家。

speaker: Unknown
en: I was for 25 years a professor at Caltech, California Institute of Technology.
zh: 我曾在加州理工学院担任了 25 年的教授。

speaker: Unknown
en: I had a lab studying the biophysics of the brain, but also cognitive neuroscience and the way people see and experience.
zh: 我有一个实验室,研究大脑的生物物理学,同时也研究认知神经科学,以及人们如何看待和体验世界。

speaker: Unknown
en: And as you mentioned, I worked for 14 years with Francis Crick.
zh: 正如你提到的,我与 Francis Crick 共事了 14 年。

speaker: Unknown
en: The Nobel Prize winning molecular biologist who discovered, you know, co-discovered the double helical nature of the DNA and then shifted as he went from England to La Jolla in Southern California, shifted his interest from molecular biology to consciousness.
zh: 那位获得诺贝尔奖的分子生物学家,你知道,共同发现了 DNA 的双螺旋结构,然后随着他从英格兰搬到南加州的 La Jolla,他把兴趣从分子生物学转向了意识。

speaker: Unknown
en: I left Caltech.
zh: 我离开了加州理工学院。

speaker: Unknown
en: 15 years ago to join the Paul Allen Institute.
zh: 15 年前加入了 Paul Allen 研究所。

speaker: Unknown
en: Paul Allen, the co-founder of Microsoft for brain science here in Seattle.
zh: 也就是微软的联合创始人 Paul Allen 的脑科学研究所,在 Seattle 这里。

speaker: Unknown
en: I was a chief scientist and then its president.
zh: 我曾是首席科学家,然后是它的总裁。

speaker: Unknown
en: I've stepped down from executive duties.
zh: 我已经从行政职务上退下来了。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm still employed at the Allen Institute.
zh: 我仍然受雇于 Allen 研究所。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I also run a foundation called the Tiny Blue Dot Foundation.
zh: 我还运营着一个名为 Tiny Blue Dot Foundation 的基金会。

speaker: Unknown
en: based in Santa Monica to study perception, what we call the perception box and its therapeutic benefits for all people.
zh: 总部在 Santa Monica,研究知觉,也就是我们所说的知觉盒子,以及它对所有人在治疗上的益处。

speaker: Unknown
en: So that's briefly my biography.
zh: 这就是简要的我的个人经历。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, so as scientists, you are a physicalist.
zh: 是的,作为科学家,你是一个物理主义者。

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, it used to be known as materialist until early the 20th century, an ancient metaphysical position.
zh: 嗯,在 20 世纪早期之前它曾被称为唯物主义,这是一个古老的形而上学立场。

speaker: Unknown
en: Democritus is one of the first pre-Socratic Greek thinker.
zh: Democritus 是最早的前苏格拉底希腊思想家之一。

speaker: Unknown
en: He famously said, all there is is atoms and the void.
zh: 他有句名言:一切存在的只有原子和虚空。

speaker: Unknown
en: And today this is called physicalism that essentially asserts everything is physical.
zh: 今天这被称为物理主义,它本质上断言一切都是物理的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Put differently, everything is quantities, is numbers.
zh: 换句话说,一切都是量,是数字。

speaker: Unknown
en: The devil's in the details.
zh: 魔鬼藏在细节中。

speaker: Unknown
en: And what used to be called physical or material, if we go back to materialism, was very simple to understand on a classical physics.
zh: 而过去被称为物理的或物质的东西,如果我们回到唯物主义,在经典物理学的框架下是非常容易理解的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So on a classical physics, you take an object like this, you know, this is one of these things to, you know, train your muscles, and it has position and velocity and momentum.
zh: 在经典物理学中,你拿一个像这样的物体,你知道,这是那种用来锻炼肌肉的东西,它有位置、速度和动量。

speaker: Unknown
en: And anything that has a position in a momentum under classical physics, you can completely determine its course, its past and its future.
zh: 而任何在经典物理学下有位置和动量的东西,你都可以完全确定它的轨迹,它的过去和它的未来。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if you knew the location and momentum of every particle in the universe, everything would be an open book.
zh: 而如果你知道宇宙中每一个粒子的位置和动量,一切都会是一本打开的书。

speaker: Unknown
en: In principle, if you had a big enough computer, you can compute everything that happened in the past and everything that you expect to happen in the future.
zh: 原则上,如果你有一台足够大的计算机,你可以计算出过去发生的一切,以及你预期未来会发生的一切。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now, of course, we know the world is not described by classical physics because one of the two revolutionary theories of the 20th century is quantum mechanics.
zh: 当然,现在我们知道世界不是由经典物理学描述的,因为 20 世纪两大革命性理论之一就是量子力学。

speaker: Unknown
en: So now we have this underlying thing that cannot be directly observed, the wave function, and the wave function is interpreted in a probabilistic way.
zh: 所以现在我们有了这个无法被直接观察的东西，即波函数，而波函数是以概率的方式被解释的。

speaker: Unknown
en: and then of course to get from wave function to real things happening you have the so-called the collapse of the wave function and you've got these weird paradoxes that are very paradoxical for us to understand because we don't observe them at our level things like can be simultaneously in two states so Schrödinger's cat experiment where the cat is simultaneously dead
zh: 然后当然，要从波函数得到真实发生的事情，你就有所谓的波函数坍缩，而且你还会遇到这些非常悖论的奇怪佯谬，因为在我们的层面上我们观察不到它们，比如可以同时处于两种状态，就像薛定谔的猫实验，猫同时是死的

speaker: Unknown
en: And alive.
zh: 又是活的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And our intuition tells us, well, look, either you're dead or the cat's alive.
zh: 而我们的直觉告诉我们，好吧，你看，要么猫死了，要么猫活着。

speaker: Unknown
en: It can't be in both states.
zh: 它不可能同时处于两种状态。

speaker: Unknown
en: But under certain conditions, this is exactly what nature permits.
zh: 但在某些条件下，这恰恰是大自然所允许的。

speaker: Unknown
en: More recently, although this goes back to Erwin Schrödinger, he had predicted this property of quantum system called entanglement.
zh: 更近一些时候，尽管这可以追溯到埃尔温·薛定谔，他预言了量子系统的这种属性，叫做纠缠。

speaker: Unknown
en: What we mean, so if you have a system, a single quantum mechanical system, and this relates to consciousness already, a single quantum mechanical system, you can separate them over vast distances, but they're still one system.
zh: 我们的意思是，如果你有一个系统，一个单一的量子力学系统——这已经和意识有关了——一个单一的量子力学系统，你可以把它们分开到极其遥远的距离，但它们仍然是一个系统。

speaker: Unknown
en: What do I mean by that?
zh: 我这么说是什么意思？

speaker: Unknown
en: So let's say you take a pair of entangled particles, one is spin up and the other spin down.
zh: 比如说你取一对纠缠的粒子，一个是自旋向上，另一个是自旋向下。

speaker: Unknown
en: So because they're in a superposition, the system could be like this, it's in a superposition of this state and this state.
zh: 因为它们处于叠加态，这个系统可能是这样，它处于这个状态和这个状态的叠加态。

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay, and you don't know which.
zh: 好的，而你不知道是哪一个。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then you move them very far apart, let's say a light year, such that you turn on a flashlight at one location, that light wouldn't get to the other location until a year later.
zh: 然后你把它们分开非常远，比如说一光年，以至于你在一个地点打开手电筒，那束光要到一年之后才会到达另一个地点。

speaker: Unknown
en: So they're really, really, really far apart.
zh: 所以它们真的、真的、真的相距非常遥远。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yet,
zh: 然而，

speaker: Unknown
en: What we know now to be true empirically, beyond a doubt, that as soon as something interacts with that one system, let's say the system on my left, and knows that the spin is up, instantaneously, independent of the distance, the state of the other one is down.
zh: 我们现在凭经验确凿无疑地知道，一旦某个东西与那一个系统发生相互作用，比如说在我左边的那个系统，并且得知自旋是向上的，那么瞬时地、与距离无关，另一个系统的状态就是向下的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now, did Einstein famously call this in 1935 spooky action at a distance?
zh: 那么，爱因斯坦在 1935 年不是著名地把这称为“鬼魅般的超距作用”吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Because what mechanism allows the information, the state to propagate across vast distances?
zh: 因为是什么机制使得这个信息、这个状态能够跨越遥远的距离传播？

speaker: Unknown
en: And now there are even a weirder thing called quantum contextuality that people are testing.
zh: 而现在甚至还有一个更奇怪的东西叫做量子上下文相关性，人们正在对它进行检验。

speaker: Unknown
en: We know this to be true because now we have an industry called quantum computer industry that exploits some of these weird superposition.
zh: 我们知道这是真的，因为现在我们有一个叫做量子计算机的产业，它利用了这些奇怪的叠加态中的一部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: But what that means is that we don't know anymore what it means exactly to be physical.
zh: 但这意味着我们不再知道“物理的”究竟意味着什么了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And some people in the foundation of physics, in fact, are now arguing that there may not be absolute facts in the sense that
zh: 事实上，物理学基础领域的一些人现在正在论证，可能不存在绝对的事实，意思是

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm a biker.
zh: 我是个骑行者。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't own a car.
zh: 我没有汽车。

speaker: Unknown
en: I have several bikes.
zh: 我有好几辆自行车。

speaker: Unknown
en: My bike at rest has a particular mass.
zh: 我的自行车静止时具有一个特定的质量。

speaker: Unknown
en: It weighs like, I don't know, 25 kilo or whatever.
zh: 它大概重，我不知道，25 公斤左右吧。

speaker: Unknown
en: But quantum mechanics would say until and unless something interacts with that bicycle.
zh: 但量子力学会说，除非并且直到某个东西与那辆自行车发生相互作用，

speaker: Unknown
en: It doesn't have, probably speaking, a math.
zh: 否则它不具有——大概地说——一个质量。(译注：原文"math"疑为"mass"之误，此处照原样译出则为“一个数学”) 更正——依铁律照搬原文错误：[[78]] 否则它就不具有，大概地说，一个数学(math,原文如此)。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's not that you don't know the math, that's just an epistemic limitation.
zh: 并不是说你不知道那个数学，那只是认识论上的局限。

speaker: Unknown
en: We, you know, I don't know most things in the world.
zh: 你知道，世界上大多数的事情我都不知道。

speaker: Unknown
en: No, it's that it simply doesn't make sense to talk about it like it has a specific math until, depending on the reading, either something observes it or otherwise interacts with it.
zh: 不，而是说，在——取决于解读——要么有某个东西观察它、要么以其他方式与它发生相互作用之前，谈论它具有一个特定的数学根本就是没有意义的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now, again, this is not my grandfather's materialism anymore.
zh: 再说一次，这已经不是我祖父那个年代的唯物主义了。

speaker: Unknown
en: So that's been one persistent challenge.
zh: 所以这一直是一个持续存在的挑战。

speaker: Unknown
en: And in fact, some physicists in foundational physics are now bringing in consciousness.
zh: 而事实上，基础物理学领域的一些物理学家现在正把意识引入进来。

speaker: Unknown
en: They are beginning to argue that consciousness, in a sense, has to be built into the rock bottom, the rock bottom description of our reality.
zh: 他们开始论证，在某种意义上，意识必须被构建到最底层，即我们对实在描述的最底层之中。

speaker: Unknown
en: So the demarcation line between...
zh: 所以……之间的分界线

speaker: Unknown
en: Physicalist and non-physicalist is very, very difficult to define.
zh: 物理主义者和非物理主义者之间的分界线是非常非常难以定义的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so people say, well, it's a future physics.
zh: 于是人们说，好吧，那是未来的物理学。

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, okay, but the future physics, you know, that's like waiting for, you know, waiting for the rapture.
zh: 嗯，好吧，但未来的物理学，你知道的，那就像在等待，你知道，在等待“被提”。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, maybe in future we'll have a physics and maybe that includes consciousness for all I know.
zh: 是啊，也许将来我们会有一个物理学，也许那个物理学包含了意识，谁知道呢。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it's difficult to pin down physicalism.
zh: 所以很难把物理主义钉死。

speaker: Unknown
en: The other challenge with physicalism has always been what the philosopher David Chalmers calls the heart problem.
zh: 物理主义面临的另一个挑战，一直都是哲学家 David Chalmers 所说的“难问题”(heart problem)。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: To explain why is it that three pounds of brain matter like this.
zh: 去解释为什么像这样三磅重的脑物质，

speaker: Unknown
en: And in principle, it's just like another piece of matter like this.
zh: 而原则上，它就像另一块这样的物质一样。

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay, this is hard matter or semi-hard matter.
zh: 好的，这是硬物质或半硬物质。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is, you know, soft matter, squishy matter.
zh: 而这是，你知道，软物质，软乎乎的物质。

speaker: Unknown
en: But in principle, it's constituted out of atoms and molecules and electrons and all of that interacting by the laws of quantum mechanics.
zh: 但原则上，它是由原子、分子、电子等等构成的，它们按照量子力学的定律相互作用。

speaker: Unknown
en: Nothing special here.
zh: 这里没有任何特别之处。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yet, this thing can love and hate.
zh: 然而，这个东西却能爱能恨。

speaker: Unknown
en: Well...

speaker: Unknown
en: Where does that come from?
zh: 这是从哪来的？

speaker: Unknown
en: And even if you take it down, even if you carry out the program that Francis Crick and I initiated in the early 1990s of identifying for any one experience, what are the exact neurons in what state do they have to be?
zh: 即使你把它拆解掉，即使你执行 Francis Crick 和我在 1990 年代初启动的那个计划——为任何一种体验找出，具体是哪些神经元、它们必须处于什么状态？

speaker: Unknown
en: Do they have to involve microtubule or superposition or whatever you want to come up with?
zh: 它们必须涉及微管或者叠加态，或者你能想出来的任何东西吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Why is it that this particular mechanism, you know, it's a mechanism like any other mechanism, like a fancy Swiss clock.
zh: 为什么恰恰是这个机制，你知道，它就是一个机制，和其他任何机制一样，就像一个精巧的瑞士钟表。

speaker: Unknown
en: Why is it that this mechanism can feel pain or feel pleasure?
zh: 为什么这个机制能感受到痛苦或快乐？

speaker: Unknown
en: Or feel boredom.
zh: 或者感受到无聊。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, it's a complete non sequitur, right?
zh: 我是说，这完全是一个不相连的推论，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: On the one hand, you have the laws of physics.
zh: 一方面，你有物理定律。

speaker: Unknown
en: On the other hand, you have experiences, pain, pleasure, boredom, anger.
zh: 另一方面，你有体验，痛苦、快乐、无聊、愤怒。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know they're linked.
zh: 你知道它们是相互关联的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Just a single hit on the head will tell you, yeah, if you hurt the brain, you're going to seriously interfere with conscience.
zh: 只要在头上敲一下你就会明白，是的，如果你损伤了大脑，你就会严重干扰 conscience。

speaker: Unknown
en: But why should they be linked?
zh: 但为什么它们应该被关联起来？

speaker: Unknown
en: There's nothing in the laws of science that tells us matter can love and hate.
zh: 科学定律中没有任何东西告诉我们物质能够爱和恨。

speaker: Unknown
en: So those are the two challenges.
zh: 所以这就是两大挑战。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I mean, they've been around for several decades now.
zh: 我是说，它们已经存在几十年了。

speaker: Unknown
en: The neural correlates, exactly what was lighting up at the time that you were feeling or experiencing certain phenomena.
zh: 神经相关物，也就是当你感受或体验某些现象时，究竟是什么在亮起。

speaker: Unknown
en: And at what point did you decide...
zh: 那么你是在什么时候决定……

speaker: Unknown
en: That that wasn't going to be enough.
zh: 那不会是足够的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, I guess you knew that wasn't going to be enough, but you thought it was useful in the absence of some other empirical experiment that... Well, assuming we had the... And of course, I lost the famous bet against David Chalmers because we had not discovered them after 25 years, but he agrees with me, they will be discovered.
zh: 我是说，我想你知道那不会是足够的，但你认为在没有其他实证实验的情况下它是有用的……嗯，假设我们有那个……当然，我输掉了与 David Chalmers 的那场著名赌局，因为 25 年后我们还没有发现它们，但他同意我的看法，它们会被发现的。

speaker: Unknown
en: This isn't discovering the...
zh: 这并不是发现那个……

speaker: Unknown
en: Footprints of consciousness in the brain is another way to think about them.
zh: 大脑中意识的足迹，这是看待它们的另一种方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: That is a perfectly feasible project and that will be immensely useful because once I know what the footprints are, I can look for them.
zh: 那是一个完全可行的项目，而且会极其有用，因为一旦我知道足迹是什么，我就可以去寻找它们。

speaker: Unknown
en: For instance, there are many patients that are behavioral unresponsive.
zh: 例如，有许多行为上无反应的病人。

speaker: Unknown
en: They used to be called vegetative state.
zh: 他们过去被称为植物人状态。

speaker: Unknown
en: We now know that 25% of these people are actually conscious, called covert conscious.
zh: 我们现在知道，这些人中有 25% 实际上是有意识的，这被称为隐性意识。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're fully conscious, or they may be fully conscious, we simply don't know, but we can't communicate, they can't communicate that to the outside, so they're like a standard astronaut, okay?
zh: 他们是完全有意识的，或者可能是完全有意识的，我们只是不知道，但我们无法沟通，他们无法向外界传达这一点，所以他们就像一个标准的宇航员，好吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, if I have the NCC, I can just look, are they present in this patient?
zh: 那么，如果我拥有 NCC，我只需要查看，它们在这个病人身上存在吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: I can decide, for example, most people, most experts who concern themselves would assume that a third trimester fetus probably is conscious.
zh: 我可以判断，例如，大多数关注这个问题的人会假设孕晚期的胎儿很可能是有意识的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, if I have the NCC, I can say, well, are they there?
zh: 那么，如果我拥有 NCC，我就可以说，嗯，它们在那里吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Or when do they occur?
zh: 或者它们什么时候出现？

speaker: Unknown
en: Are they present already in the second trimester or maybe only in the third trimester?
zh: 它们在孕中期就已经存在了，还是只在孕晚期才有？

speaker: Unknown
en: What about here?
zh: 那这里呢？

speaker: Unknown
en: I have a dog, a Bernice Mound dog.
zh: 我有一只狗，一只 Bernice Mound dog。

speaker: Unknown
en: What about dogs?
zh: 那狗呢？

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, and I can, so...
zh: 你知道，我可以，所以……

speaker: Unknown
en: This is an empirical program tracking the footprints of consciousness that will be immensely practical importance to the term consciousness, to measure it, to maybe quantify it in normal people, in people with various diseases, disorders, psychiatric disorders, animals, etc.
zh: 这是一个追踪意识足迹的实证项目，将对意识这个术语具有极其重要的实用价值——去测量它，也许去量化它，在正常人身上，在各种疾病、失调、精神疾病的患者身上，在动物身上，等等。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it's useful, but of course it does not explain why
zh: 所以它是有用的，但当然它并不能解释为什么

speaker: Unknown
en: This particular thing in this configuration gives rise to red and slightly different to orange or to an orgasm or to a toothache, right?
zh: 这个处于这种特定构型的东西会产生红色，而稍微不同的构型产生橙色，或者产生性高潮，或者产生牙痛，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: So there are two ways to look at that.
zh: 所以有两种方式来看待这个问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: So one for the longest, you have to start rather...
zh: 其一，在很长的时间里，你必须从……开始

speaker: Unknown
en: So most people who think about consciousness and make theories of consciousness, they take the brain and try to squeeze the juice of consciousness out of it.
zh: 所以大多数思考意识并构建意识理论的人，他们拿起大脑，试图从中榨出意识的汁液。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, they're trying to turn the waters of the brain into the wine of consciousness to adopt a biblical metaphor.
zh: 你知道，他们试图把大脑的水变成意识的酒，借用一个圣经的比喻。

speaker: Unknown
en: And they say, well, it has to be this thing.
zh: 然后他们说，嗯，必须是这个东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: It has to be a global workspace or broadcast of information or layer five neurons or NMDA receptors or microtubule like Stu Hameroff, you know, or whatever.
zh: 它必须是全局工作空间，或者信息的广播，或者第五层神经元，或者 NMDA 受体，或者像 Stu Hameroff 说的微管，你知道的，或者其他什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, again, why this and not that?
zh: 可是，再说一次，为什么是这个而不是那个？

speaker: Unknown
en: Why microtubulein and not some other cellular organism?
zh: 为什么是微管蛋白而不是某种其他细胞生物体？

speaker: Unknown
en: Ultimately, it's very difficult to go beyond that question.
zh: 归根结底，很难越过这个问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: So there's one theory that's unique, really, that's called integrated information theory.
zh: 所以有一个理论确实是独一无二的，它叫整合信息理论。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's a different attack.
zh: 这是另一种攻击。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's a consciousness first account.
zh: 它是一种意识优先的论证。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it really starts where Rene Descartes started.
zh: 所以它实际上是从勒内·笛卡尔开始的地方出发的。

speaker: Unknown
en: The only thing I'm absolutely certain of is that I'm conscious.
zh: 我唯一绝对确定的事情，就是我有意识。

speaker: Unknown
en: Because even in doubting it, I reassert it.
zh: 因为即使我在怀疑这一点，我也在重新确立它。

speaker: Unknown
en: And consciousness, furthermore, is the only way I encounter the world.
zh: 而且，意识还是我遭遇世界的唯一方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: If I'm a scientist, I still depend on, I have to read papers or books, that's visual consciousness.
zh: 如果我是一个科学家，我仍然依赖于——我必须读论文或书，那是视觉意识。

speaker: Unknown
en: I have to look at an oscilloscope again.
zh: 我必须再看一眼示波器。

speaker: Unknown
en: I have to listen to a Geiger counter, that's auditory consciousness.
zh: 我必须听盖革计数器，那是听觉意识。

speaker: Unknown
en: So the only way I interact with the world, including my own body, is through my conscious experience.
zh: 所以我与世界互动的唯一方式，包括我自己的身体，都是通过我的意识体验。

speaker: Unknown
en: So if you think about it, the only thing I have direct acquaintance with, I have direct knowledge of, is conscious experience.
zh: 所以你想一想，我唯一有直接相识的、有直接认知的东西，就是意识体验。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so any theory has to start with any theory of consciousness.
zh: 所以任何理论——任何关于意识的理论——都必须从这里开始。

speaker: Unknown
en: Which is different from a theory of the neural correlates, the physical substrate of consciousness.
zh: 这不同于关于神经相关物、意识的物理基质的理论。

speaker: Unknown
en: Any theory of consciousness has to start with consciousness and then sort of go from there to say, well, which system is conscious and what are they conscious of?
zh: 任何关于意识的理论都必须从意识出发，然后从那里推出去，说：好，哪些系统是有意识的，它们意识到的是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: And this theory, integrated information theory, the main architect of that theory is an Italian-born American psychiatrist and neuroscientist, Giulio Tononi at the University of...
zh: 而这个理论，整合信息理论，它的主要架构者是一位意大利出生的美国精神病学家和神经科学家，朱利奥·托诺尼，在……大学。

speaker: Unknown
en: Wisconsin-Madison is a theory that does that.
zh: 威斯康星-麦迪逊，就是这样一个理论。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now, it's a scientific theory.
zh: 现在，这是一个科学理论。

speaker: Unknown
en: It may well be wrong.
zh: 它很可能是错的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 嗯。

speaker: Unknown
en: Let me ask, first of all, I'm fascinated by, you have a startup, right, that's working on an instrument or instruments that would be able to detect consciousness in people who are otherwise considered brain dead.
zh: 让我先问一下，我很好奇，你有一家初创公司，对吧，正在研发一种或多种仪器，能够检测那些通常被认为脑死亡的人的意识。

speaker: Unknown
en: How far along have you gone in that?
zh: 这方面你们进展到什么程度了？

speaker: Unknown
en: Have you abandoned that?
zh: 你放弃了吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Oh, no, no, no.
zh: 哦，不，不，不。

speaker: Unknown
en: As I said, it's just independent of what you believe about the metaphysics of consciousness.
zh: 正如我所说，这独立于你对意识形而上学持什么信念。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's no question that we have now tools, so this was developed over the last 20 years, techniques to query the brain.
zh: 毫无疑问，我们如今有了工具——这是在过去20年里发展起来的——用于探询大脑的技术。

speaker: Unknown
en: Essentially, you do it, you hit the brain using magnetic pulses, and then you're sounding, you're listening to the echoes using EG.
zh: 本质上，你是这样做的：用磁脉冲敲击大脑，然后用脑电图（EG）监听回声。

speaker: Unknown
en: Electrical brainwaves, right?
zh: 电脑波，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: So you send in a pulse of energy, you essentially, you know, it's like taking a bell and hitting it with a hammer and then listening to it.
zh: 所以你送入一个能量脉冲，本质上，你知道，就像拿起一口钟，用锤子敲它，然后听它的响声。

speaker: Unknown
en: And a conscious brain, whether that person is awake like you or I, or in a REM sleep where the person is experiencing, or on a high dose psychedelic where they may be immobile but highly conscious, the complexity of this brainwave, so you can compute...
zh: 而一个有意识的大脑，无论那个人是像你我一样清醒，还是处于做梦的快速眼动睡眠中——那个人正在体验着什么，还是摄入高剂量致幻剂——他们可能无法动弹但意识高度清醒——这种脑波的复杂度……你可以计算——

speaker: Unknown
en: How complex is called Lempel-Ziv, complexity.
zh: 复杂度有多高，叫做 Lempel-Ziv 复杂度。

speaker: Unknown
en: And in conscious people, it's always...
zh: 而在有意识的人身上，它总是……

speaker: Unknown
en: Above a threshold.
zh: 高于某个阈值。

speaker: Unknown
en: In unconscious people, whether they're regular people, regular folk, but they're anesthetized, or they're truly in a very deep coma where it's unambiguous that there is no activity, the brain complexity is very low.
zh: 而在无意识的人身上——无论是普通人，被麻醉了，还是真正处于极深的昏迷、毫无疑问没有活动的状态——大脑复杂度都非常低。

speaker: Unknown
en: In the simplest case, EG is flat-lined.
zh: 最简单的情况下，脑电图是拉平的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, that's an extreme case of very low complexity.
zh: 我是说，那是极低复杂度的一个极端例子。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so we've developed this tool now.
zh: 所以我们现在开发出了这个工具。

speaker: Unknown
en: And started this company that you mentioned called Intrinsic Powers, where we're working with people at MGH, at Harvard and in Madison and in Columbia, trying to put this into the workflow.
zh: 并创办了你提到的这家公司，叫 Intrinsic Powers，我们正在与麻省总医院（MGH）、哈佛、麦迪逊和哥伦比亚的研究人员合作，试图把它纳入临床工作流程。

speaker: Unknown
en: Because what happens today is if you or I have a car accident or hemorrhage or cardiac arrest,
zh: 因为今天的情形是：如果你或我遭遇车祸、大出血或心脏骤停，

speaker: Unknown
en: And you're alive.
zh: 而你还活着。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, someone calls 9-11, you get into the ICU, you're on life support now, on ventilator.
zh: 你知道，有人打9-11，你被送进重症监护室（ICU），你现在靠生命维持系统、靠呼吸机。

speaker: Unknown
en: You might be there, you know, unresponsive, eyes open.
zh: 你可能就那样待着，没有反应，眼睛睁着。

speaker: Unknown
en: So these people were called vegetative states, but as I said, are now called behavioral unresponsive.
zh: 这些人以前被称为植物人状态，但正如我所说，现在被称为行为无反应。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if you remain in this state for three or four or five days, then the clinical team will initiate discussion with the family and says, is this what they would have wanted?
zh: 而如果你保持这种状态三四五天，临床团队就会与家属展开讨论，说：这是他们想要的吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: And here, in the developed world, between 70 and 90 percent of the time, family and doctors decide no and they pull support.
zh: 而在发达国家，70% 到 90% 的情况下，家属和医生会决定不，然后撤除支持。

speaker: Unknown
en: But we now know that a quarter of these patients, there was a very large paper last year published in the New England Journal of Medicine, roughly a quarter percent, depending on the demographics and all of that, one out of four of these patients is actually conscious, they're there, they're present.
zh: 但我们现在知道，这些病人中有四分之一——去年《新英格兰医学杂志》发表了一篇非常大的论文——大约四分之一，取决于人口统计等各项因素，这些病人中每四人就有一个实际上是有意识的，他们在那里，他们存在。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're just not able to signal it.
zh: 他们只是无法发出信号表达。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so we want to know that because then I can give this device can give the clinical team and the family one additional bit.
zh: 所以我们想知道这一点，因为这样，这个设备就能给临床团队和家属多提供一比特的信息。

speaker: Unknown
en: Literally, it's one bit.
zh: 字面上说，就是一比特。

speaker: Unknown
en: Are they there or are they not there?
zh: 他们在那里，还是不在那里？

speaker: Unknown
en: And that can then help further inform, you know, what the doctor and what the family wants to do with that information.
zh: 而这可以进一步帮助医生和家属就如何处理这一信息做出决定。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I like it a lot because, well, A, we help people and B, demonstrate that this very airy, ephemeral topic of consciousness, you know, it's been around with us for the last 3,000 years, seems very airy-fairy, right?
zh: 所以我很喜欢这件事,因为,嗯,A,我们帮助了人们,B,证明了意识这个非常飘渺、转瞬即逝的话题——你知道,它已经伴随我们三千年了——看起来非常虚无缥缈,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: But this...
zh: 但这个……

speaker: Unknown
en: If you ever called upon this to make this call for a loved one, this is the most consequential decision you can make.
zh: 如果你曾经被打电话要求为你所爱的人做出这个判断,这是你能做出的最重大的决定。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's very existential.
zh: 这是非常关乎存在的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Are they there or are they not there?
zh: 他们在还是不在?

speaker: Unknown
en: And should we pull the plug or not?
zh: 我们该不该拔掉插头?

speaker: Unknown
en: And so this is where this abstract mind-body problem hits the road.
zh: 所以这就是这个抽象的心身问题落地的地方。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是啊。

speaker: Unknown
en: And let me just, I don't want to get lost on that, but how far have these experiments gone?
zh: 让我……我不想在这个话题上陷得太深,但这些实验进行到什么程度了?

speaker: Unknown
en: If you have someone in a vegetative state who's been declared in a vegetative state, and you use this device and detect that there is complex neural activity that suggests consciousness, if you
zh: 如果有一个人被宣布处于植物人状态,而你用这个设备检测到存在表明意识的复杂神经活动,如果你

speaker: Unknown
en: Pull the life support on that patient.
zh: 撤掉那个病人的生命维持。

speaker: Unknown
en: Do you see some spike in complexity that might correlate to their recognition of what's happening?
zh: 你会看到复杂度出现某种峰值,可能与他们对正在发生的事情的认知相关吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: Or do you see any change in that complexity?
zh: 还是你会在那个复杂度上看到任何变化?

speaker: Unknown
en: No, because I mean, the technique is, so it takes an hour, an hour and a half to establish.
zh: 不会,因为,我的意思是,这项技术需要一个小时到一个半小时来建立。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then, of course, you know, you'll have to make this information available to the doctors and ultimately to the team.
zh: 然后,当然,你知道,你必须把这些信息提供给医生,最终提供给整个团队。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then it takes, you know, a lot of back and forth.
zh: 然后需要,你知道,大量的反复沟通。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's complicated, Craig, because it's a very complicated question and we cannot help.
zh: 这很复杂,Craig,因为这是一个非常复杂的问题,而我们无法提供帮助。

speaker: Unknown
en: So there are three, when you get that call, there are three things you want to know.
zh: 所以有三件事,当你接到那个电话时,有三件事你想知道。

speaker: Unknown
en: Are they alive first?
zh: 首先他们还活着吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: Are they there?
zh: 他们在吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: And then lastly, are they going to recover?
zh: 最后,他们会康复吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: And right now, we can't say that very well, whether or not the fact that they're conscious is encouraging, even though they may not be able to respond.
zh: 而现在,我们无法很好地回答,他们有意识这一事实是否令人鼓舞,即使他们可能无法做出反应。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it's a very difficult decision to make.
zh: 所以这是一个非常难做的决定。

speaker: Unknown
en: Do you think...
zh: 你认为……

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, imagine yourself, if you are in this situation, unable to communicate, and it's unclear, it depends, of course, on your age, if you're 20, it's much better than if you're, you know, 60 or 70.
zh: 我的意思是,想象一下你自己处于这种境地,无法沟通,而这不明朗,当然,这取决于你的年龄,如果你是 20 岁,那比你是,你知道,60 或 70 岁要好得多。

speaker: Unknown
en: What would you like?
zh: 你会想要什么?

speaker: Unknown
en: Do you want to be forever in this state where you can't communicate, but you're conscious?
zh: 你想永远处于这种无法沟通、但你却有意识的状态吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: And then, you know, now your brother or your sibling, I mean, or your parent or your child has to make this decision.
zh: 然后,你知道,现在你的兄弟或你的兄弟姐妹,我是说,或者你的父母或你的孩子必须做出这个决定。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it's a very complicated decision environment.
zh: 所以这是一个非常复杂的决策环境。

speaker: Unknown
en: And because at this point, we can't tell you, yes, he's there and 95% chance he's going to recover.
zh: 因为在这一点上,我们无法告诉你,是的,他在,而且有 95% 的几率他会康复。

speaker: Unknown
en: I can't tell you that.
zh: 我无法告诉你那个。

speaker: Unknown
en: So was that work concurrent with your work with Crick?
zh: 那么那项工作与你和 Crick 的工作是同时进行的吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, so this was primarily done, you know, this work on patients sort of widely published, done over the last 20 years by Giulio Tononi and then an Italian neuroscientist, neurologist, Marcello Massimini.
zh: 是的,这项工作主要是,你知道,这项关于病人的研究被广泛发表,是在过去 20 年里由 Giulio Tononi 以及一位意大利神经科学家、神经病学家 Marcello Massimini 完成的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, and that went on at the same time.
zh: 是的,那是同时进行的。

speaker: Unknown
en: as we try to push this empirical program in people and in lab animals to study the footprints of consciousness in the brain.
zh: 正如我们试图在人和实验动物身上推进这个实证项目,以研究大脑中意识的足迹。

speaker: Unknown
en: A purely empirical program that, by the way, does not depend on whether you're a physicalist or dualist or a panpsychist or an idealist.
zh: 一个纯粹实证的项目,顺便说一下,它不取决于你是物理主义者、二元论者、泛心论者还是唯心论者。

speaker: Unknown
en: We just want to know the footprints of consciousness, how to study them, how to measure them, detect them.
zh: 我们只是想知道意识的足迹,如何研究它们,如何测量它们、检测它们。

speaker: Unknown
en: We could then use for diagnostic and prognostic purposes.
zh: 我们随后可以将其用于诊断和预后目的。

speaker: Unknown
en: At what point did you decide that you were never going to close that gap between correlation and causality and switch to a form of panpsychism?
zh: 你是在什么时候决定你永远不会弥合相关性和因果性之间的鸿沟,并转向某种形式的泛心论的呢?

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, was it, I guess, was it a moment or is it, was it?
zh: 我是说,那是一个,我猜,是一个时刻,还是……是吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, first of all, I don't, I've never abandoned the hope that we can get a theory that explains, I mean, a theory like integrated information theory and, you know, panpsychism, certainly the way I think about it is in the sense that it may well be possible
zh: 嗯,首先,我不,我从未放弃我们能得到一个解释性理论的希望,我是说,像整合信息论这样的理论,而且,你知道,泛心论,当然我的思考方式是在这个意义上,即很有可能

speaker: Unknown
en: A, that every member, every evolved organism, including simple cells, individual cells, a mobile, may feel like something, itsy bitsy, okay?
zh: A,每一个成员,每一个进化出来的生物体,包括简单的细胞、单个细胞、一个 mobile,都可能有某种感觉,哪怕微不足道,好吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: And integrated information theory in principle, because the vast complexity of the 10,000s of different proteins present even in a single cell is such no computers ever managed to simulate that.
zh: 而整合信息论原则上——因为即使在一个单细胞中存在的一万种不同蛋白质的巨大复杂性——是任何计算机都从未成功模拟过的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Out of all this vast complexity may arise some very, very simple proto-feeling of being alive as is not being alive.
zh: 在所有这些巨大的复杂性中,可能产生某种非常非常简单的原初感觉,即活着与不活着的感觉。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's entirely possible.
zh: 这完全是可能的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't know how to empirically test it right now, but it's entirely possible.
zh: 我现在不知道如何从实证上检验它,但它完全是可能的。

en: What happened to me is slightly different.

speaker: Unknown
en: Some people have it weaker, they constantly belittle themselves, you know, they constantly think, oh my God, everyone hates me.
zh: 有些人的自我感较弱，他们不断贬低自己，你知道，他们总是想，天哪，所有人都恨我。

speaker: Unknown
en: And other people, like our president, have a, let's just call it a highly exaggerated sense of self.

en: It's always about me, me, me, explicitly, implicitly.
zh: 永远都是我、我、我，无论是显性的还是隐性的。

speaker: Unknown
en: But then just like an astronaut on a special condition can become weightless and floating out of space, so on certain conditions, including psychedelics, of course, you can totally lose that self.
zh: 但就像宇航员在特殊条件下可以失重并漂浮在太空中一样，在 certain 条件下，当然包括致幻剂，你可以完全失去那个自我。

speaker: Unknown
en: And what you realize then, that self-consciousness is just a subset of all possible experiences.
zh: 而那时你会意识到，自我意识只是所有可能体验中的一个子集。

speaker: Unknown
en: The fact that I know I'm me, I know what I had for breakfast, I know I'm going to die one day, all of that is consciousness, but you can also, if you don't have that, like in that state, whatever remains is clearly highly conscious.
zh: 我知道我是我，我知道我早餐吃了什么，我知道自己总有一天会死，所有这些都是意识，但你也可以，如果你没有那些，就像在那个状态中，无论剩下的是什么，显然都是高度有意识的。

speaker: Unknown

zh: 然后它消除了我对死亡的恐惧，这并不罕见。

speaker: Unknown

zh: 但后来我有了第二次体验，它并没有从根本上改变我的形而上学，即我看待世界的方式。

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown

zh: 而且，你知道，自希腊人以来，大多数人都说，嗯，真正存在的唯一一极是物质，其他一切都必须以我们不理解的某种方式从中涌现出来。

speaker: Unknown

en: It's independent of what you think about it.

zh: 我们可以俯视它。

speaker: Unknown
en: But the question is, does the machine by itself, is it meaningful?
zh: 但问题是，机器本身，它有意义吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: No.
zh: 没有。

speaker: Unknown
en: And all it does, it just takes whatever it gets and then it predicts the next thing and the next thing and the next thing and does it amazingly well.
zh: 它所做的，只是拿它得到的东西，然后预测下一个东西、下一个东西、再下一个东西，而且做得惊人地好。

speaker: Unknown
en: I grant all of that.
zh: 这些我都承认。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's clearly passed the Turing test, but that doesn't mean it feels like anything.
zh: 它显然已经通过了图灵测试，但这并不意味着它有任何感受。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay, well, I've taken up more than an hour of your time.
zh: 好吧，我占用你超过一个小时的时间了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Where are you going next?
zh: 你接下来要做什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: You're working on the quantum... Yeah, we're doing experiments on... Yeah, that's one thing.
zh: 你在做量子……是的，我们在做关于……是的，这是一件事。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm just really interested in it.
zh: 我只是真的对此很感兴趣。

speaker: Unknown
en: I always thought the chances are very small, and I still think the chances are very small, but the great thing about science and nature is if you ask the right scientific question to nature, you will get the right answer.
zh: 我一直认为机会很小，我至今仍认为机会很小，但科学和自然的伟大之处在于，如果你向自然提出正确的科学问题，你就会得到正确的答案。

speaker: Unknown
en: You will get an answer, and this is what we claim, what it can tell us about nature, so that's a great thing.
zh: 你会得到一个答案，这就是我们所主张的，它能告诉我们关于自然的什么，所以这是一件很棒的事。

speaker: Unknown
en: You have to design the right experiment to test this, but then you will get an answer one way, so we will know sooner or later, whether it's going to be on my watch or not, who knows.
zh: 你必须设计正确的实验来检验这一点，但之后你迟早会得到一个方向的答案，所以我们迟早会知道，是不是在我有生之年，谁知道呢。

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay.
zh: 好的。
